claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys are primarily governed by local microstructural order and deposition-induced lattice strain.
Rapid thermal annealing can induce nanoscale disorder and refine grain boundaries in the proposed FeMnNiGeSi alloy.
Appropriately controlled rapid thermal annealing can avoid full phase decomposition.
Annealing-induced disorder and grain-boundary refinement will broaden the sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
Broadening the transition will reduce hysteretic losses while retaining a high magnetic entropy change.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited alloy has a coarse microstructure typical of arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons.
A short-dwell anneal below the ordering temperature will selectively reduce short-range order without changing overall composition.
The proposed intervention is a moderate-temperature, short-dwell rapid thermal anneal.
Rapid thermal annealing will reduce local lattice strain while partially disrupting long-range order.
Reduced lattice strain and disrupted ordering will transform the abrupt first-order transition into a more gradual transition.
A more gradual transition will distribute the entropy change over a broader temperature window.
The annealing-induced microstructure will reduce magnetic-domain-wall pinning and thereby lower hysteresis.
Rapid thermal annealing and grain-boundary refinement will increase the effective surface-to-volume ratio and improve heat exchange.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will have a broader and less hysteretic transition.
Annealed samples will retain a similarly high overall magnetocaloric effect.
Annealed samples will exhibit improved heat-exchange characteristics.
The baseline alloy undergoes a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The predictions are limited to similarly deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys treated with moderate annealing conditions.
The annealing temperature and dwell time required to generate useful disorder without reducing magnetocaloric capacity are unknown.

contradictions.description: The target is alternately described as an as-deposited material, an arc-melted ingot or melt-spun microribbon, and either a film or bulk sample. These processing forms have substantially different geometries and microstructures, so they do not define a consistent baseline.

The proposed grain-boundary refinement is said to enhance effective surface-to-volume ratio and heat exchange, but internal grain-boundary refinement does not necessarily increase the external surface-to-volume ratio governing heat transfer. No geometry-changing intervention is specified.
